new_state.retire_valid: One committed ring slice has been copied into descriptor. A zero-keep slice may occupy it for one cycle.
new_state.retire_has_data: Known0/1 procedural classification of captured read_keep!=0, registered together with descriptor.

combinational_equations: All existing read_count, committed/occupied and both capacity arithmetic branches unchanged; capacity uses this new retire. No read_keep/read_any/current payload in retire_room or retire_pop.

Existing public valid_o = enabled && active_o && output_valid is unchanged. It does not combinationally mask prospective fault_now. The old registered public beat may handshake on a fault edge; the edge then clears future ownership.
clock_priority: Asynchronous reset initializes original state plus retire_valid=0, retire_has_data=0. Descriptor payload reset tozero in its separate asynchronous-reset writer for deterministic startup; it remains unobservable while retire_valid=0.
Original flush_i || stream_start_i branch clears retire_valid and retire_has_data and all original owners. Flush dominates simultaneous start exactly as V17.
Original (stream_abort_i && active_o) || fault_now branch clears retire_valid and retire_has_data along with original ring/output ownership. No next-cycle stale descriptor release is allowed.
In the existing active, nonfault branch: clear output_valid if output empty or ready; if retire_pop and retire_has_data, load existing output data/metadata from old descriptor and set output_valid.

In that same active branch: if retire_pop set retire_valid=0; if retire set retire_valid=1, default retire_has_data=0 then if(read_keep!=0) set it1. Capture wins over simultaneous pop, so old descriptor reaches output while replacement becomes owned.

Advance original read_ptr by old read_count exactly when retire. Copy all read payload fields into descriptor in a separate posedge/asynchronous-reset writer gated by retire. It may copy values on a simultaneous parser/header/capacity fault but the priority branch clears descriptor validity; those bytes cannot become visible before a fresh valid capture rewrites every field.

All original parser state/CRC/commit/verdict events, input bank state and original seven ring writes stay in their original priority positions. The original retire output-load block is the only output data source replaced.

EDS drain completion becomes original ending && read_ptr==write_ptr && !retire_valid && (!output_valid || ready_i). This prevents the last descriptor from being discarded before it reaches the output; existing stream_end pulse/active clear and output valid clear remain once-only.
latency_and_throughput: An eligible ring slice captured at edge n can reach the public output register at edge n+1. This is one explicit internal cycle beyond V17 for a no-stall empty-pipeline stream; no cycle-equivalence claim.

Pop and capture are simultaneous when descriptor and output can progress. Therefore sustained capacity is four DWORD slots /16 byte positions perclock, same as parser and original wide interface. Capture/pop availability is independent of newly selected ring payload.

A zero-keep descriptor pops even when a nonzero public output is held with ready=0. While such empty descriptors replace one another, the ring continues freeing four slots percycle after at most one initial stage cycle; this must be witnessed under the aligned DLLP/IDL test.

One additional descriptor increases maximum buffered retirement capacity by up tofour DWORD slots. Under permanent nonempty-output stall, overflow is still required; its exact cycle may move later. Never reduce ring depth or assume incoming physical line can be backpressured.

When input epochs are accepted without overflow, CRC/verdict event order and values and accepted raw-word cadence are unchanged. Output beat grouping under stalls may change, so validate per-byte sequence and metadata plus event counts rather than old cycle timestamps.

For faulted epochs, bytes actually handshaken before or on the fault edge remain delivered; all unaccepted ring/descriptor/output bytes are canceled at that edge. This is explicit existing sampling-edge fault policy; scoreboard must model it and reject old-epoch data after restart.
invariants: Every descriptor owned byte originated from an old-state committed ring slot with a resolved good verdict and its matching data/metadata; invalid/unknown-masked slots contribute zero keep.

A ring slot may be overwritten after read_ptr advances only because every selected descriptor field has been copied atomically. The new writer has a single owner and writes all six fields on the same edge.
Descriptor and existing output each have independent valid/has-data ownership; no nonempty descriptor is overwritten while output is stalled, and no bytes duplicate on simultaneous pop/capture.
When valid output is held under ready-low and no reset/start/flush/abort/fault edge occurs, all public beat fields remain stable.
On every control epoch boundary descriptor_valid, ring occupancy and outputvalid clear with the original priorities; invalid descriptor contents may differ but cannot escape.

Original slot_verdict invariant, tag wrap and packet quarantine apply unchanged at the read capture boundary. Unknown literal payload bits are copied through mux/register as before; no OR reduction of selected payload.
An EDS pulse is forbidden while descriptor_valid or an unconsumed public beat remains. No data appears after EDS until explicit restart.
